findings.reason: without a dispatch precondition a node reads a half-built wave, and the record it writes cannot be the population its own done-when claims, so the node has to be redispatched and its first record discarded.
findings.text: §12's done-when fixes its population as "the wave's runs are the query's whole population", but §12 is marked `implementable` and neither `plan-section-depends-on` (which has no `s12` entry) nor the section's prose gates its dispatch on the wave having landed; §8 carries exactly that sentence for its own node ("this section's node is dispatched only once every arm has its count") and §12, which measures a smaller wave the coordinator is producing right now, has no equivalent

findings.reason: the threshold names the wrong precondition, so the rule fires on some populations where the statistic exists and stays silent on some where it does not, and a node following it literally either divides by zero or silently drops a split, biasing the reported spread downward.
findings.text: the control's escape reads "With fewer than four baseline runs the record states that the control could not be taken and why", keyed on the count of baseline *runs*, while the statistic it guards is cumulative input per *landed node*: a split half of two runs in which neither landed has zero landed nodes, so the difference is undefined and the plan states no disposition, and because the escape clause itself satisfies the done-when a node can close the section having produced no comparison at all

findings.reason: one word decides whether the number in the record is a spread or a maximum, and the wrong reading changes every arm figure's stated scale.
findings.text: the control asks the record to report "the largest of those splits' differences in cumulative input per landed node", but a difference between two halves is a signed quantity and "the largest" of three or ten signed differences is not a spread: the most negative split is discarded, so the reported same-arm spread is an upper-tail figure that can understate the very noise it exists to show

response_events.note: §12 now states its node is dispatched only once every run of the wave has landed or been closed

wiring-1.note: §12 now states its node is dispatched only once every run of the wave has landed or been closed

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every section reference in §12 (§5, §8, §10) resolves to a section that exists, the named fragment target `docs/evidence/fragments/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node/interim-arm-report.html` sits in a directory holding ten sibling fragments, and the codex fixtures §8's imported controls name (`docs/research/fixtures/codex-refused-patch-stream.jsonl`, `codex-anchored-edit-stream.jsonl`) are present.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the "fewer than four baseline runs" escape is keyed on run count while the control's statistic needs landed nodes, so a record can satisfy the done-when with no comparison at all.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the record sits at `docs/evidence/fragments/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node/interim-arm-report.html`, a durable in-repo path whose directory already holds ten sibling fragments.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §12 names no symbol, module or function, and carries no plan label, ticket number or version tag into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (too few quiet open sections for §8's counts) matches the evidence it cites in its own Why, the endpoint (a per-arm table plus a same-arm spread) is obtainable from the run store and run directories, and the section prescribes no implementation.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §12 delivers one artifact, the interim evidence record; the wave is explicitly the coordinator's work, not the node's.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §12 measures a wave the coordinator must produce but declares no depends-on, gate or dispatch precondition for that wave, and is declared `implementable`, so the queue can dispatch it while the wave is still running.
